status_summary: On TikTok the record runs opposite to the recommendation: the 2024 divest-or-ban law took effect on 2025-01-19, five executive orders (14166, 14258, 14310, 14350 and 14352) delayed its enforcement, and Executive Order 14352 (signed 2025-09-25) determined that a framework for a U.S. joint venture was a qualified divestiture, with ByteDance holding under 20 percent; the joint venture closed on 2026-01-22 with ByteDance at 19.9 percent, and the app was not banned. On Confucius Institutes, the House passed H.R. 881 on 2025-05-07 to cut off DHS funds to schools tied to them, and earlier defense authorization acts already restrict Defense Department funding for hosting universities; no new enacted outlawing of Confucius Institutes was found. On other equipment, the FCC added foreign-produced drones and certain listed Chinese-linked communications equipment to its Covered List on 2025-12-22, a parallel step covered in c28-03.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14166 delays enforcement of the divest-or-ban law (Public Law 118-50, Division H) until 2025-04-05; Executive Orders 14258, 14310 and 14350 later extend the delay to 2025-06-19, 2025-09-17 and 2025-12-16 in turn.

The House passes H.R. 881, the DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act, which would require schools to sever ties with Confucius Institutes and certain Chinese entities or lose Department of Homeland Security funding, subject to a national security waiver; no Senate action was found.

President signs Executive Order 14352 (published 2025-09-30), determining that a divestiture framework creating a U.S.-based TikTok joint venture, majority-owned by U.S. persons with ByteDance and affiliates under 20 percent, is a qualified divestiture, and directing the Attorney General not to enforce the Act for 120 days.

The FCC Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau adds all foreign-produced drones and drone critical components, and certain communications and video surveillance equipment listed in section 1709 of the FY2025 defense authorization law, to the Covered List.

The TikTok U.S. joint venture deal, valued at $14 billion, closes; Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX hold 15 percent each and ByteDance keeps 19.9 percent, and the House China committee chair says the committee will oversee the deal.

title: Outlaw Confucius Institutes, TikTok and other Chinese propaganda and espionage arms
uncertainties: The TikTok joint venture closing date (2026-01-22) is from a Politico report republished by Yahoo Finance and is consistent with a GMA Network report of 2026-01-24; the joint venture terms were read in the executive order and news reports, not in the transaction documents, and whether the algorithm is licensed from ByteDance was not reported. The H.R. 881 vote tally and Senate status were not found, and the text of the bill was not read. The earlier defense authorization funding restrictions (FY2019 and FY2021) are described by a 2022 advocacy tracker and are not new actions in the tracked period; FY2026 defense authorization provisions were not checked. The Covered List step covers all foreign-produced drones, not only Chinese ones. In review, diverged was kept over a low proposed rating because the most specific item, TikTok, was not outlawed: enforcement of the existing ban law was suspended for about a year and the app continues under a divestiture with a retained ByteDance stake, while the Confucius Institute bill has passed only the House. Related record c28-03 covers the FCC and TikTok in more detail.
